threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, editing, inspection, repair, scrubbing and PDF/PNG rendering engine, exposed through the native CLI, PyO3/Python facade and CLI, optional Python MCP stdio server, and wasm-bindgen browser/Node byte APIs. Documents enter package admission, OPC/XML parsing and comparison/edit/render components; outputs return as bytes or are published by the host adapter. Legacy DOC conversion is a separate OLE parser (src/lib.rs:7-29; src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:5-15; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-98). Native rendering additionally reads host fonts and maintains a persistent font index; it is not entirely filesystem-free (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2276,2637-2652,3090-3106,3213-3229). Conditional privileged paths are explicitly requested CLI self-update and maintainer release publication (src/update.rs:186-258; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-369; scripts/release.sh:886-899).
assets: Confidential document text, comments, authors, embedded media and generated reports; MCP returns document-derived text and inspection data to its connected client (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-217).

Integrity of source snapshots, exact edit targets, resulting tracked changes and published files. PlanV2 validates source.sha256 before resolving decisions, scope and operations (src/edit/v2_apply.rs:80-106).

Host filesystem authority: native CLI ambient output paths; MCP's independently held directory capability; Markdown's separately granted image-resource capability (src/publication.rs:146-225; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2870).
Process memory/CPU availability across Rust, Python and WASM consumers; package admission budgets are not complete process-resource isolation (src/admission.rs:39-99; SECURITY.md:71-74).

Host font files and persistent font-index integrity. The index records looked-up families, source-file paths and filesystem stamps, and subsequently reads those paths (src/convert/font.rs:3090-3096,3154-3171,3192-3227).

Installed native executable, release assets, GitHub publication authority, optional signing-key material and registry publication credentials (src/update.rs:198-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919,935-954,1069).
trustBoundaries: Document supplier to engine: supplied DOCX ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, embedded fonts/images and Markdown are data, not operator configuration. Representative comparison and rendering paths admit packages before processing; admission checks ZIP structural disagreement and package identity (src/document_comparer.rs:4907-4927; src/convert/mod.rs:773-778; src/admission.rs:439-490). Defaults are 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB inflated, 10,000 entries and depth 256; comparison permits 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated (src/admission.rs:63-99).

Raw XML caller to DOM: parse_xdocument is deliberately permissive and does not enforce input policy; checked try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates before DOM construction. Do not collapse these independently exposed APIs into universal automatic admission (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:90-108,119-135). Debug is a deliberate unchecked ZIP-inspection path, distinct from production package refusal (src/opc/archive.rs:16-45; src/debug.rs:213).

MCP client to document filesystem: --root defaults to server cwd and is expanded/resolved once. _OutputRoot holds cap-std directory authority; actual reads and publication use that authority, rather than trusting Python's earlier resolve checks. All connected callers receive the registered read/write tools; annotations are hints, not user/tenant authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1276; src/publication.rs:146-199).

MCP write capability: tool-selected out_dir derives clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json and optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png beneath the root. Native publication rejects unsafe relative names, escaping resolution and output symlinks; overwrite must be requested. Staging is validated before commits, but atomicity is per file and failures can report prior committed files (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217; src/publication.rs:123-130,168-199,228-250,431-469,558-569).

CLI operator to ambient filesystem: native publication holds each explicitly selected parent directory, stages bytes in parent/.jubarte-<uuid>.partial/bytes and installs by rename or no-clobber hard link. This grants ambient local access, unlike OutputRoot. Python and npm CLIs instead perform their own ambient direct writes after overwrite checks; shared command grammar does not establish equal filesystem guarantees (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225,480-505,558-569; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-103,126-133,510-517; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79,106-111).

Markdown image reference to host file: native CLI --resource-path overrides the Markdown source's parent directory, defaulting to '.'. URL-like targets are refused; decoded/canonicalized paths must resolve inside that root and actual reads use its held OutputRoot capability. This is separate from document output publication (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2669-2677,2811-2848,2858-2870,2937-2943).

Native renderer to ambient font resources: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform user-font locations; system/Word/Office cloud-font directories are also searched. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index path; empty/off disables it; otherwise the default is user_font_dir().parent()/font-index.tsv. Index writes use sibling font-index.tsv.<pid>.tmp followed by rename, outside the MCP document-root capability when the configured font location is outside it (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2235,2281-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3100-3106,3213-3229). Effective default font directories are macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts else $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. The default index is one directory above, font-index.tsv. Windows system font roots use WINDIR else SystemRoot else C:\Windows, plus LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts; Office cloud cache is $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts.

JS host to WASM: compare accepts borrowed document bytes plus JSON limit overrides and returns bytes/errors. Browser/Node package entrypoints are separate generated loaders; native publication is cfg-excluded on wasm32. Node CLI filesystem authority belongs to its JS adapter, not to the WASM byte API (jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:65-98; jubarte-wasm/npm/package.json:34-75; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-55,106-111).

Operator to updater to release infrastructure: only explicit self-update enters this flow. Fixed repository jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, target-specific asset and SHA256SUMS.txt feed self_update; --check does not install; confirmation or --yes precedes installation. RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so this checkout enforces checksum-only updates. A regular-file verification hook rejects extracted symlink/nonregular binaries before swap (src/update.rs:25-48,186-210,223-257,307-321). Windows enables ZIP extraction while other shipped targets use tar.gz (Cargo.toml:144-155; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:25-36). Archive assets are jubarte-<version>-<target>.tar.gz or .zip, containing jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]; current executable replacement is delegated to self_update and its consumer implementation requires verification.

Maintainer/tag authority to public distribution: v* tags trigger release builds; build jobs have contents:read and release job contents:write. Optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is provided to the signing step, decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and removed by trap; signed archives precede checksum generation. GH_TOKEN references GITHUB_TOKEN for gh release create, publishing dist/* to the tagged repository release. The maintainer script separately publishes crates.io jubarte-redlines, npm jubarte-wasm and jubarte-redlines, and PyPI jubarte-redlines using operator-held credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-308,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:886-899,919,935-954,1069).
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier may control document package bytes, XML, embedded fonts/images, Markdown and edit-plan content passed by a host. The supplier does not thereby control environment variables, the MCP root, arbitrary CLI flags, release assets, signing keys or operator credentials (SECURITY.md:38-74; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-87; src/update.rs:25-48).

An authorized MCP client can request registered document reads and writes anywhere allowed by the granted root and tool parameters, including overwrite=true. This already-authorized root access is not a new privilege; a meaningful failure would cross the root or other independently enforced capability (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75-108,152-160).

A caller embedding the Rust/Python library already has its host process's authority. Parser-input compromise could add unauthorized access or computation, but no repository evidence establishes an internet-facing or multitenant deployment (src/lib.rs:7-11; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:5-15).

Release-asset replacement becomes relevant only when an operator requests an update; checksum-only authenticity depends on the trusted release channel because an asset replacer can also replace its adjacent checksum. Signing-key or release-workflow compromise is a distinct privileged prerequisite (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-257).

A separate local filesystem adversary may control entries in an operator-selected shared output/plan directory without permission to write victim-owned files elsewhere. Direct writes and predictable staging add capability if they follow those entries; private directories prevent this scenario (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133,407-411; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-112,420-423).
securityObjectives: Treat the inputs named by repository policy as untrusted; preserve admission, ZIP/XML constraints and checked parsing boundaries, and require host memory/CPU limits rather than treating input budgets as isolation (SECURITY.md:38-74; src/admission.rs:63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:129-135).

Keep untrusted document processing from fetching external relationships or executing document macros; retain the policy's distinction between permitted ambient host resources and external document references (SECURITY.md:71-85; src/admission.rs:22; src/opc/mod.rs:778). The engine crate forbids unsafe Rust; this does not claim dependency-wide absence of unsafe code (src/lib.rs:86).

Preserve edit-source identity and exact scope before mutation, then preserve publication target and payload integrity with the guarantees owned by the particular adapter (src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-106; src/publication.rs:168-173,538-569).

Confine MCP document reads/writes and native Markdown image reads to their independently granted capabilities; do not advertise these as whole-process confinement of native rendering (src/publication.rs:146-199; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2870; src/convert/font.rs:3100-3106,3213-3229).

Permit executable replacement and public package publication only through the separately authorized operator/maintainer workflows; preserve platform/asset selection, checksum verification and the actual configured signature policy (src/update.rs:186-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-308,356-369; scripts/release.sh:886-899).
assumptions: No supplied threat model, deployment context or knowledge base. Root SECURITY.md was resolved as applicable; no nested SECURITY.md was found. Architecture review was independent, offline/read-only, without application execution, network, triggering inputs or a vulnerability audit.

No observed server deployment, HTTP listener, authentication layer, tenant isolation, process sandbox or host CPU/memory quotas is established. The supported MCP entrypoint uses stdio; its host must choose an appropriate root and trust connected clients accordingly (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; SECURITY.md:72-85).

Documentation qualification: src/lib.rs:9-11 describes every function as package-byte processing with no temporary files, and MCP prose says every path/output is under root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:7-9). Native rendering actually reads ambient fonts and writes the persistent font index and sibling temporary file (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3213-3229). Document capability confinement remains distinct from those renderer side effects.

Documentation qualification: Python/npm CLI descriptions advertise the same output files and behavior as the native binary, but their direct path writes do not inherit native cap-std staging and no-clobber installation. Parent review established shared-directory attacker prerequisites for separate retained findings (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:5-7,126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:6-8,106-111; src/publication.rs:558-569).

Documentation qualification: signing support is implemented but currently inactive; do not describe releases from this checkout as signature-required. docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-80 agrees with empty RELEASE_KEYS and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None in src/update.rs:44-48.

Documentation disagreement: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 says GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN lift updater request limits; src/update.rs:198-211 configures neither auth_token nor auth_token_from_env. Independent reviewer inspected cached self_update 1.3.1 defaults None/false, so ambient updater token transmission is not established. Supporting dependency evidence from reviewer: self_update-1.3.1/src/backends/github.rs:358-359 and src/backends/common.rs:1027-1053; parent has not fully audited the dependency.

jubarte-rust-inproc is a developer benchmark worker, not a separate production service: stdin COMPARE paths cause ambient file reads and output writes under harness authority (jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,91-99).

Registry/package-manager authentication, actual signing-secret availability, branch/tag protection and deployments outside this repository remain external prerequisites; the model does not establish their live settings.

Input resource constraints are byte/depth/count based; semantic renderer amplification and relationship normalization are investigated separately. One focused investigator failed to return; parent continued source validation directly.

findings.title: Python CLI follows output symlinks and bypasses atomic no-overwrite protection
findings.summary: Writing Python CLI outputs in an attacker-writable directory can create or truncate another file through a destination symlink. `_ensure_writable()` checks existence separately and `_write()` follows links with `Path.write_bytes()`. Bundle members reach the same writer.

severity.rationale: A local attacker controlling entries in a selected output directory can redirect a more privileged user's write outside that directory. Corrupting victim-owned configuration or documents has high integrity impact, but shared-directory access and a victim invocation are prerequisites. No remote exposure is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: An enforced private output directory would substantially reduce likelihood; privileged unattended processing of shared directories would increase it.

confidence.rationale: Current source directly shows the CLI entry, symlink-following existence guard and truncating writer. No runtime reproduction was run; platform protections may restrict specific deployments.

codeEvidence.label: Diff output argument reaches publication
codeEvidence.code:
def cmd_diff(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Text only, as in the native CLI: the patch, a text view, or (two
    Markdown documents) CriticMarkup, on stdout or in -o's file."""
    from . import _native
    from .document import _decode_diff

    output = args.output
    # An existing output is refused before any work.
    if output is not None:
        _ensure_writable(output, args.force)
    old = _read_side(args.old, args.old_format)
    new = _read_side(args.new, args.new_format)
    if args.format in ("github", "word", "normal", "context", "side-by-side"):
        text = _native.diff_view(old, new, format=args.format, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                 context=args.context, accept_changes=args.accept_changes, full_lines=args.full_lines)
    else:
        critic = args.format == "critic"
        if critic and not (isinstance(old, str) and isinstance(new, str)):
            raise CliError("--format critic needs both documents in Markdown; "
                           "`jubarte compare OLD NEW` prints their redline as the agent view")
        # The shared parser dated the run (D17).
        text = _decode_diff(_native.diff_json(old, new, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                              author=args.author, date=args.datetime, columns=args.columns, critic=critic)).text
    if output is None:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return EXIT_OK
    size = _write(output, text)
codeEvidence.explanation: The user-selected output passes an early existence check, then engine work occurs before `_write(output, text)`, leaving the destination unreserved.

codeEvidence.label: Nonatomic overwrite guard
codeEvidence.explanation: `Path.exists()` follows symlinks and does not reserve the pathname. Dangling links appear absent; a concurrent substitution also bypasses this precheck.

codeEvidence.label: Direct output open follows the destination link
codeEvidence.explanation: `Path.write_bytes(raw)` opens the output with truncation and follows a symlink, so the attacker-selected referent receives the victim's output bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Bundle members use the same writer
codeEvidence.code:

    for name, data in outputs:
        _write(out_dir / name, data)
        saved.append({"f": name, "bytes": len(data), "sha256": _native.source_sha256(data)})
    lines.append(_jsonl({"ev": "save", "dir": str(out_dir), "outputs": saved}))

codeEvidence.explanation: Each engine-produced bundle member and report goes through `_write`, so preplanted member links under a forced bundle reuse the same broken control.

codeEvidence.label: Documented output and plan authority
codeEvidence.code:
The CLI intentionally grants ambient local authority to explicitly requested
paths. It replaces an output symlink itself, not the link's target. Recording
a plan through a symlink retains its documented local behavior: the link stays
in place and its resolved plan file is atomically replaced. Plan recording
uses exclusive staging but concurrent read/modify/write recordings remain
last-writer-wins, not a serialized append or compare-and-swap.
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented CLI contract authorizes the output pathname and says output symlinks are replaced themselves. The Python direct open instead writes through them.

rootCause.summary: The output's no-clobber decision is detached from its creation, and the final writer lacks exclusive creation or rename-based replacement. A writable directory entry therefore determines the victim's eventual filesystem sink after authorization.

findings.remediation: Expose and use the existing native publication API for Python CLI outputs, passing overwrite authorization into the commit operation. Preserve atomic no-clobber behavior and replace destination symlinks rather than opening their referents.

counterEvidence: This requires attacker influence over an output-directory entry; an untrusted DOCX alone does not select the destination.
The CLI intentionally permits explicitly requested ambient local paths, but that does not authorize an attacker-selected symlink referent.
The native Rust publisher uses private exclusive staging and rename or atomic no-clobber hard-link installation; the Python CLI does not call it.
The MCP adapter separately uses native OutputRoot capability operations and is not affected by this Python CLI sink.
limitations: Requires attacker control of the selected destination directory; private directories prevent this path.
OS sticky-directory protections can narrow exploitability.
validation.summary: Verified the Python diff handler and edit-bundle caller reach the direct writer; there is no staging publisher or no-follow/exclusive flag at the sink. A dangling output link can create an unintended file without `--force`; an existing victim file can be targeted with `--force` or a directory-entry race.

dataflow.summary: CLI output argument → _ensure_writable() uses Path.exists() → conversion, rendering or diff generation → _write() uses Path.write_bytes(), which opens with truncation and follows symbolic links.

reachability.summary: The attacker needs writable entries in the chosen output parent but need not be able to modify the target file directly. The victim runs the Python CLI and has write access to that target.
reachability.attacker: A local attacker able to create or replace entries in the chosen output directory, such as a shared workspace, without permission to modify a victim-owned target elsewhere.
preconditions: Shared or attacker-writable chosen output directory.
Victim has write access to target file.
For an existing target, --force or a substitution after the precheck; a dangling link can create a new target without force.

attackPath.summary: A local attacker places or substitutes an output symlink in a directory used by a victim CLI invocation; the final direct open follows it.

remediationTests: Integration test a destination link with and without overwrite authorization; only the directory entry may be replaced.
Race a destination creation between preparation and commit; no-clobber must fail atomically.
Test forced bundle members that are symlinks.

findings.title: npm CLI follows output symlinks and bypasses atomic no-overwrite protection
findings.summary: Writing npm CLI outputs in an attacker-writable directory can create or truncate a different file through a destination symlink. `ensureWritable()` checks existence separately and `write()` follows links with `fs.writeFileSync()`. Bundle members use the same sink.

severity.rationale: A local attacker controlling entries in a selected output directory can redirect a more privileged user's write outside that directory. Corrupting victim-owned configuration or documents has high integrity impact, but shared-directory access and a victim invocation are prerequisites. No remote exposure is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: An enforced private output directory would substantially reduce likelihood; privileged unattended processing of shared directories would increase it.

confidence.rationale: Current source directly shows the CLI entry, symlink-following existence guard and truncating writer. No runtime reproduction was run; platform protections may restrict specific deployments.

codeEvidence.label: Diff output reaches direct publication
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected output passes `ensureWritable` before engine work and is later forwarded to `write`; the pathname is not reserved.

codeEvidence.label: Separate overwrite check
codeEvidence.explanation: `existsSync` follows links and cannot enforce no-clobber at commit. Dangling links appear absent.

codeEvidence.label: Truncating output open follows links
codeEvidence.explanation: `fs.writeFileSync(file, data)` uses default truncating write semantics and follows the destination symlink to its referent.

codeEvidence.label: Bundle files share direct writer
codeEvidence.explanation: Edit-bundle members and report use `write` as well, retaining the same symlink-following sink for forced directory reuse.

codeEvidence.label: CLI publication contract
codeEvidence.code:
The CLI intentionally grants ambient local authority to explicitly requested
paths. It replaces an output symlink itself, not the link's target. Recording
a plan through a symlink retains its documented local behavior: the link stays
in place and its resolved plan file is atomically replaced. Plan recording
uses exclusive staging but concurrent read/modify/write recordings remain
last-writer-wins, not a serialized append or compare-and-swap.
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented CLI behavior is replacement of the symlink itself, with exclusive staging, which this host writer bypasses.

rootCause.summary: The npm host authorizes output absence before processing inputs, then opens the mutable directory entry directly with truncation. No exclusive create, held directory publication or rename separates the authorized pathname from an attacker-selected symlink referent.

findings.remediation: Implement host-side publication using exclusive private staging and atomic rename for forced replacement, with an atomic no-clobber commit when force is false. Hold or otherwise protect the selected parent directory across publication and do not open destination symlink referents.

counterEvidence: This is a local filesystem attack requiring control of the selected output directory or its entries.
Existing ordinary files are refused without --force when no concurrent substitution occurs.
Ambient CLI path access is intentional; following an attacker-substituted destination link is the unauthorized behavior.
The native Rust publisher has stronger controls, but the npm host performs its own filesystem writes.
limitations: Requires control of selected output directory entries; private directories prevent this attack.
Platform symlink protections can restrict particular deployments.
validation.summary: Verified npm diff and bundle paths call the same direct writer. Existing files are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case, but dangling links pass the check, while forced output or a concurrent link replacement reaches the symlink-following open.

dataflow.summary: CLI output argument → ensureWritable() checks fs.existsSync() → engine work → write() calls fs.writeFileSync() with its default truncating, symlink-following mode.

reachability.summary: The attacker controls entries in the chosen output parent and the victim can write the referent. An existing-file attack needs --force or a race after the precheck; a dangling link permits unintended file creation without force.
reachability.attacker: A local attacker able to create or replace entries in the chosen output directory, such as a shared workspace, without permission to modify a victim-owned target elsewhere.
preconditions: Victim CLI invocation with write permission to the selected target.

attackPath.summary: A local attacker plants or substitutes an output symlink before a victim's npm CLI write; the direct open uses the victim's filesystem authority.

remediationTests: Integration test a destination link with and without overwrite authorization; only the directory entry may be replaced.
Race a destination creation between preparation and commit; no-clobber must fail atomically.

findings.title: Rendering a DOCX with large table spans can exhaust the host process
findings.summary: Rendering a small DOCX table whose `gridSpan`, `gridBefore` or `gridAfter` carries a large positive integer sizes vectors from that integer. Package admission bounds bytes and XML depth, but does not bound the expanded table grid; a compact document can request gigabytes of allocation and terminate its native, Python or WASM host.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reliably request excessive allocations through a normal public rendering API without controlling the host configuration. The established impact is process availability, not memory corruption or code execution. Host memory/CPU isolation can constrain the damage and no remote/shared-service deployment is established.
severity.changeConditions: Exposure in a shared document service without worker isolation would increase operational impact; strict host isolation and semantic column budgets reduce it.

confidence.rationale: Static trace establishes the caller-controlled attribute, usize parse without an upper bound, propagation to RawCell and occupancy-driven vector expansion. No application execution or allocation experiment was performed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource consumption / numeric allocation amplification

codeEvidence.label: Public rendering opens admitted package bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: Rendering admits package bytes, normalizes strict namespaces and opens the main XML. The admission operation is structural/byte based and does not restrict grid-span numeric magnitude.

codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker-controlled main XML is parsed and its body selected for layout; the semantic table attributes remain intact.

codeEvidence.label: Body table enters table layout
codeEvidence.explanation: The body walker recognizes the table and forwards its DOM node to `table_block` before any raster page limit applies.

codeEvidence.label: Cell span has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The cell's `gridSpan` value is parsed as the returned usize, lower-bounded at one, and receives no maximum-column or allocation-budget check.

codeEvidence.label: Parsed span is used for the cell
codeEvidence.explanation: `table_block` obtains `colspan` from `cell_span` and retains it for building a RawCell.

codeEvidence.label: Row skip becomes a synthetic spanned cell

Input byte limits cannot bound this semantic expansion.

findings.remediation: Apply a configurable maximum logical table-column count and checked cumulative span arithmetic before creating any RawCell-derived dense grid. Reject oversized gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter with a typed input-limit error, and charge later column and merge vectors against the same resource budget.

findings.title: Rendering encoded relationship targets can consume quadratic CPU
findings.summary: A document relationship target containing many XML-encoded ampersands is decoded by the OPC reader and then decoded again when resolving the part. `unescape_xml_text()` searches the remaining suffix for every literal ampersand, causing quadratic work before a missing related part can be ignored. A small compressed document can stall its processing worker.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reach the decoder during normal rendering through internal header/footer/note relationships; no privileged options are required. The concrete impact is loss of process availability. Resource-isolated workers constrain impact, and an internet/shared-service deployment is not established.
severity.changeConditions: A shared processing service without worker CPU deadlines increases operational impact; eliminating the second decode or using a linear scanner removes the amplification.

confidence.rationale: Repository parser and round-trip tests establish that relationship targets are already XML-decoded. Current callers feed these decoded targets into the wrapper, and the decoder's nested suffix scans establish quadratic complexity. No runtime timing test was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Document bytes reach package parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: Normal rendering admits the package, normalizes it and opens PartFs; a valid relationships XML part is not rejected merely for a long encoded target within byte limits.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship XML is parsed by the OPC model
codeEvidence.explanation: Metadata records are forwarded to `oxml_opc::Relationships::from_xml` and their parsed items are retained, so XML attribute decoding happens before relationship consumers.

codeEvidence.label: Current-tree regression asserts decoded targets
codeEvidence.explanation: This source test documents the current model contract: an encoded ampersand in Target becomes a literal ampersand and survives subsequent package round trips.

codeEvidence.label: Normal renderer enumerates story relationships
codeEvidence.explanation: `with_layout` obtains story XML through `story_parts_xml`, reaching relationship resolution during the ordinary layout path.

codeEvidence.label: Decoded internal targets are resolved before lookup
codeEvidence.explanation: Header/footer/note/comment targets pass into `pkg.resolve_rel_target` before `part_string` checks whether a related part exists, so no huge-named target part is needed.

codeEvidence.label: Resolver redundantly XML-decodes the parsed target
codeEvidence.explanation: This wrapper claims it receives raw attributes and invokes `unescape_xml_text`, but its relationship-model callers already hold decoded strings.

codeEvidence.label: Every unsupported ampersand rescans the remaining suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: For each literal ampersand the decoder searches all remaining characters for a semicolon. If there is no supported entity it advances by only one; N literal ampersands therefore require roughly N(N-1)/2 character checks.

rootCause.summary: The PartFs relationship wrapper applies XML decoding to an already-decoded model field. That exposes a legacy decoder whose unsupported-entity path rescans the same suffix for each ampersand. Well-formed XML-encoded ampersands become a long literal-ampersand sequence after the first parse and trigger the quadratic second pass.

findings.remediation: Resolve parsed Relationship.target values directly without XML-decoding them again. Make the standalone entity decoder single-pass for unsupported/unterminated references as well, preserving its documented permissive output without rescanning suffixes.

counterEvidence: The XML/ZIP byte and attribute limits still apply, but allow targets large enough for substantial superlinear work.
External relationships are not fetched; this is CPU consumption before in-memory part lookup, not SSRF.
Normal checked XML text rejects unsupported entities, but valid encoded attribute ampersands decode successfully in the OPC model before the second pass.

findings.title: Rendering with a shared font-index directory can overwrite a staging-link target
findings.summary: When native rendering saves a font index in an attacker-writable directory, it writes through a predictable PID-based temporary pathname. A local attacker can place a symlink there and cause the renderer to truncate an unrelated victim-writable file before the index rename.

severity.rationale: Destructive file overwrite is possible with the renderer's user authority, but the normal index parent is a private per-user application-data directory. Exploitation additionally requires an operator-selected shared/custom index parent or weakened default permissions and knowledge of the process ID, giving low likelihood. Document input alone cannot select an arbitrary index location.
severity.changeConditions: Demonstrated use of a shared index directory in a more privileged renderer raises likelihood; enforced private ownership and exclusive staging prevent the attack.

confidence.rationale: Source directly traces native rendering to cache misses, index recording and a predictable nonexclusive fs::write. Deployment of an attacker-writable index parent is conditional, not asserted.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering performs installed-font lookup
codeEvidence.explanation: A native layout pass invokes add_installed_faces using document font names, so enabled font-index updates are a normal rendering side effect.

codeEvidence.label: Uncovered family invokes installed-font loader
codeEvidence.explanation: A painted family absent from embedded/catalogue fonts is loaded through installed_family_faces.

codeEvidence.label: Installed lookup uses persistent font index
codeEvidence.explanation: The font lookup calls indexed_faces with FONT_INDEX and a real filesystem scan closure.

codeEvidence.label: Operator configuration selects index parent
codeEvidence.explanation: The index is disabled by an empty/off setting; otherwise an environment-selected path or a sibling of the per-user font directory supplies the parent. This is trusted operator configuration, not a document path.

codeEvidence.label: Cache miss records and saves scanned results
codeEvidence.explanation: A missing or stale index entry calls index.record after the scan, so a first lookup can trigger a save even when no matching face exists.

codeEvidence.label: Recording calls save
codeEvidence.explanation: The new entry is inserted and immediately passed to the save operation.

codeEvidence.label: PID-based temporary open follows preexisting symlinks
codeEvidence.explanation: The temporary path is derived from the index path and process ID, then fs::write follows a symlink and truncates its referent. The later rename cannot undo that write.

rootCause.summary: The persistent index uses a predictable sibling pathname as if it were an exclusively owned staging file. Ordinary fs::write opens with truncation and follows links, allowing a directory-entry attacker to redirect a rendering side effect beyond the authorized index.

findings.remediation: Save the font index through exclusively created private random staging in the held parent directory, then rename the completed regular file. Preserve the index's configuration semantics without opening any preexisting temporary entry.

counterEvidence: Default per-user application-data index parents are normally private.
An attacker who only supplies documents cannot choose JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or JUBARTE_FONT_DIR.
Empty/off JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX disables this path.
Some OS symlink protections or inaccessible parent permissions prevent the attack.

validation.summary: Verified render-to-font lookup, cache-miss recording, index path precedence and predictable temporary write. No exclusive create, private staging directory or no-follow open protects the temporary entry. The index's final path is not attacker-selected by the DOCX.

candidate.title: Legacy DOC repeated piece ranges amplify logical text
candidate.originalMessage: main_text trusts logical ccp_text and expands every CP into StoryChar, while multiple monotonically increasing piece intervals can all point at the same physical fc range.
